items.text:
De hoofdvegetatie heeft inderdaad **vier boomsoorten met elk drie vaste modelvarianten**: eik, beuk, berk en grove den. Daarnaast krijgen de geplaatste bomen variatie in schaal, draaiing en kleur. Er bestaat ook nog een eenvoudiger vegetatiesysteem voor onder meer cipressen en enkele buitengebieden.

Je referenties onderscheiden zich vooral door herkenbare bladranden, samenhangende bladgroepen en duidelijke lichte bovenkanten met donkere binnenruimtes. De huidige bomen hebben al vertakte stammen, maar het loof blijft uit gesloten volumes bestaan. Alleen meer polygonen toevoegen gaat dat verschil niet oplossen.

Ik begin met de **berk, in alle drie de varianten**. Daarmee kunnen we zowel het fijne loof als de witte bast en de luchtige kroon goed toetsen aan je vierde referentie. Dezelfde aanpak moet daarna bruikbaar zijn voor de andere bomen en lagere vegetatie.

# VEG-R02 — vegetation style renewal

Status: **Birch style prototype for review. No production activation.**

Source: production branch `ccr-75ef4113-kfkimm` at `752cb02` (includes car R02). Isolated worktree/branch `veg-r02-reference-style`; other sessions' worktrees were not edited. The owner requested investigation and renewal of all outside nature, explicitly allowing one tree species first to establish the style.

## Verified model inventory

The main woodland kit (`src/world/woodkit.ts`) contains four species × three seeded structural variants = **12 tree models**, each with near/mid/far/xfar representations. These are model variants, not twelve individual planted trees. Production Hybrid uses near/mid/far with the far geometry reused for xfar, preserving the earlier VEG-R01 choice. Placement adds stable heading, scale and tint variation; saplings reuse the same tree models.

Runtime `vegList()` snapshot from the estate at this baseline:

| Family | Model variants | Placed instances in tree batch |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Oak | 3 | 456 |
| Beech | 3 | 427 |
| Silver birch | 3 | 177 |
| Scots pine | 3 | 198 |
| Hazel | 3 | 350 |
| Holly | 3 | 127 |

The diagnostic `woodCounts.trees = 1735` includes **1258 trees and 477 bushes**. It must not be described as 1735 actual trees. This includes the backdrop and 353 saplings; it excludes the separately rendered clipped cypresses. The same snapshot reports 11693 plant/litter instances, 36 scattered fallen logs, 232 rock instances (including 49 boulders). Counts describe this deterministic baseline, not an authoring target.

| Other nature | Existing implementation | Renewal direction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fern, bilberry, foxglove, lily of the valley, anemone | 3 variants each; explicit leaf/flower geometry | Broad frond shapes, flower silhouettes, readable colour patches; keep species distinct |
| Grass | 4 tuft variants; reused as tall shore grass | Curved, tapered blades; grouped heights and occasional seed heads; separate close lawn, wild verge and reed treatments |
| Hazel and holly | 3 variants each; branch skeleton + mostly closed crown masses | Share the leaf-spray shading language; different outline, leaf shape and density |
| Stumps | Shared flared body and sawn top; plain, absorbed and nurse treatments | Irregular break/saw profiles, readable rings, bark rim and integrated moss; retain collision fit |
| Fallen/cut trunks | 4 scattered log size/seed variants plus bespoke placed timber | Bark/end-grain consistency with trees, capped branch stubs, broken tips and moss patches |
| Branches, root flares, split timber and log seats | Tree skeletons and separately authored props | One bark vocabulary, coherent taper, connected branch junctions and grounded placement |
| Leaf litter | Separate instanced fallen-leaf model | Species-shaped leaves and calm patches; avoid fine noise everywhere |
| Mushrooms | Legacy caps/stems and local authored decorations | Intentional cap silhouettes and clustered arrangements; audit garden remnants too |
| Garden cypresses | Legacy `nature.ts` cone construction, not woodland variants | Dedicated clipped evergreen model; do not confuse with Scots pine |
| Box hedges / legacy garden flowers | Separate `estate.ts` geometry and some `nature.ts` instances | Controlled clipped outline with fine edge leaves; replace remaining flower blobs |
| Rocks, boulders, exposed earth and shore | Seeded rocks, authored terrain/verge/contact layers | Broad planes, restrained material breakup and embedded contact; coordinate moss with dead wood |

Inventory is intentionally broader than `woodkit.ts`: changing that file alone would miss outdoor nature. Water/sky are neighbouring systems, not vegetation replacements in this workstream.

## Reference analysis and direction

The four user references rely on three scales working together: a legible whole-tree silhouette; overlapping, asymmetrical foliage groups; and small leaf tips/gaps at the edge. Bark and branching remain readable between groups. Warm outer/top leaves and cooler, darker interiors make crowns volumetric. The meadow works through patches and quiet space, not uniformly scattered decoration.

Adopt those relationships while retaining the project's European woodland species and earthy green palette. The blue/purple/yellow trees in the references demonstrate form/material variation; they are not an instruction to recolour the estate as a fantasy biome.

## Implemented birch prototype

- All three birch variants use new leaf sprays instead of closed polygonal clumps.
- Slightly hanging, overlapping sprays make a connected, fuller crown. Trunk/branch geometry, placements, colliders and the shared deterministic tree-layout stream are retained.
- A deterministic 512×512 shared cutout texture provides separate rounded, pointed leaf shapes and internal gaps. Five crossed planes per foliage group at near, three at mid/far. This keeps macro structure while reducing close detail with distance.
- Colour/normal shaping carries crown volume. The existing shared tree material, multi-draw and instanced fallback architecture are retained.
- The cutout is applied in a matching custom depth material on both vegetation batching paths, so high-quality sun shadows follow leaves rather than opaque rectangles.
- Explicit experiment selector: `?vegstyle=birch-r02`, optionally `&multidraw=0`. Production/default stays on the existing models. This prototype has not been merged or deployed.

An initial individual-leaf mesh trial was discarded: it was either too airy or still exposed closed clumps and added excessive triangles. The retained spray approach substantially improves the crown at much lower geometric cost. Its alpha-tested overlapping surfaces create a **fill-rate trade-off**: triangle savings alone do not establish phone performance.

## Evidence and validation

`scripts/veg-r02-review.mjs` reproduces the six-model lineup and detail view from real Three.js geometry, matched normal-game views, both rendering paths, distance sweeps and high-quality shadow controls. `docs/veg-r02/models.json`, `inventory.json`, `results.json` and the per-path LOD sweeps are machine-readable evidence. Screenshots are actual rendered geometry, not concept images.

The three near birches have 640 / 560 / 600 leaf triangles versus 948 / 851 / 868 before, with identical wood geometry. Scene costs depend on the visible LOD mix; far/mid sprays can cost more geometry than the old reduced crowns.

Typecheck, production build and all 296 unit tests pass, including exact trunk/branch compatibility, determinism, finite geometry/normals and bounds. The existing bundle-size warning remains. Normal-game evidence and limitations are summarized in `docs/veg-r02/README.md`.

Not established: sustained physical Samsung FPS/temperature, distant leaf shimmer on that device, full puzzle-route readability with the fuller crowns, or final visual approval. No full gameplay regression pass is claimed.

## Rollout after the style review

1. Resolve birch crown density, leaf scale, palette and silhouette against the references; validate Samsung motion and fill cost before activating.
2. Give oak, beech and pine their own crown architecture and leaf/needle sprays; retain three genuinely distinct models per species. A species-wide spherical substitution would lose the reference quality.
3. Extend to hazel, holly, garden cypresses and hedges, using family-specific outlines.
4. Renew grass/reeds, ferns, bilberry and flowers as coherent ground-cover patches; retain route/clue clearances and deliberate empty space.
5. Reconcile bark, roots, branches, dead/cut wood, stumps, mushrooms, litter, rocks and moss across all outdoor code paths.
6. Validate transitions in motion, both render paths, scene budgets and actual Samsung performance. Update the inventory with explicit coverage; do not label all nature renewed after only the woodland kit changes.

De hoofdvegetatie bevat **vier boomsoorten met elk drie modelvarianten**: eik, beuk, berk en grove den. Dat zijn **12 basismodellen**, met daarnaast variatie in grootte, draaiing, kleur en detailniveau op afstand. De gesnoeide cipressen gebruiken nog een apart, eenvoudiger systeem.

Ik heb **alle drie de berken vernieuwd als eerste stijlproef**. Hieronder staan links de bestaande modellen en rechts de nieuwe:

![Bestaande en vernieuwde berken](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/c1bbbda816b1/Feh-Lu-We/docs/veg-r02/birch-lineup.png)

De nieuwe kroon heeft afzonderlijke bladranden, openingen tussen het loof en vollere, overlappende bladgroepen. De bestaande stammen en takken blijven behouden.

**Mijn beoordeling:** dit komt duidelijk dichter bij je referenties. Voor de definitieve stijl verdienen vooral de licht-donkerverdeling en het fijne bladpatroon nog aandacht; op afstand kan het loof te druk worden.

De bredere inventarisatie omvat ook:

| Onderdeel | Aangetroffen |
|---|---|
| Bosjes | Hazelaar en hulst, elk drie varianten |
| Bodemplanten | Varens, gras, bosbes, vingerhoedskruid, lelietje-van-dalen en anemoon |
| Dood hout | Gevallen stammen, gekapt hout, stronken, takken en houtobjecten |
| Overige natuur | Hagen, cipressen, riet, paddenstoelen, bladstrooisel, rotsen en mos |

Deze onderdelen staan in het [vernieuwingsplan VEG-R02](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/c1bbbda816b1/Feh-Lu-We/docs/development/workstreams/VEG-R02.md). Ze zijn **nog niet vernieuwd**; de berk dient eerst als stijlanker.

In vier gemeten gamescènes blijven de draw calls gelijk en verandert het aantal driehoeken ongeveer **−1,2% tot +1,5%**. Typecheck, build, 296 tests en vier budgetchecks slagen. Telefoonprestaties moeten nog worden getest, omdat overlappend loof extra tekenwerk vraagt.

Mag ik de prototypebranch `veg-r02-reference-style` naar `Algolon/Feh-Lu-We` pushen, zodat deze duurzaam bij het project staat?

De automatische goedkeuringscontrole blokkeerde die push omdat zij publicatie naar de repository buiten de expliciete opdracht vond vallen. Het prototype is lokaal vastgelegd; er is niets gedeployed.
